data.prompt: Insert debugging prints into your `upper_bound` function to display the values of `left`, `right`, and `centre` at the start of each loop iteration and after the loop finishes. Run the function on several test arrays and targets, then record the final values of `left` and `right`.
data.trace_question: Based on the printed trace, does the invariant you assumed (e.g., "all elements before `left` are ≤ t and all elements from `right` onward are > t") hold when the loop terminates (`left == right`)? If not, what additional condition about the loop’s termination is needed to guarantee the correct result?
data.expected_insight: You will see that the invariant alone does not guarantee correctness; you must also use the fact that the loop stops when `left == right` (the termination condition) to conclude that `left` is the smallest index with a value > t. This reveals the missing termination‑related part of the loop invariant.
